properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From Anthony's VS Code work log (SOURCE: art:vscode-call-field-log-2026-10-05, entry of 2026-10-01, "Later the same day", reflow2 0.76.0), in its words: "The hub had no written procedure for adding a member, so one was written as a project skill ... Parts of it are generic and belong in reflow2's served `hub` skill: where a member's store lives and how it stays out of an upstream repo's git (`.git/info/exclude`, never `reflow2 init` in a repo you don't own), pin shape, and 'export after every member write' under `--call`."

WHAT IS ALREADY SETTLED, so it is not re-opened:
- WHERE a design lives. dec:idea-the-design-lives-apart-from-the-implementation (accepted 2026-09-25): the design lives in its server, apart from the code it describes; for a project its owner does not control, the repository carries nothing of reflow2's; the export goes where the owner chooses. The log's "never `reflow2 init` in a repo you don't own" is that rule in practice.
- A local hub's member list is its declared dependencies. The served hub skill says so since 2026-10-02.
- Since 0.78.0 a writing `--call` exports before it exits when `--export-to` or the project's MCP configuration names the file (req:a-writing-call-keeps-the-committed-export-current). For a member store outside any project, nothing names one unless the call passes `--export-to`.
- Checked 2026-10-05 on main: the served hub skill says none of where a member's store goes, `.git/info/exclude`, a pin's fields, or exporting a member under the door. Nothing in the repository mentions `.git/info/exclude`.

THE OPEN PART is what the served text should say, and which skill should say it.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) THE REPORTER'S: an "adding a member" section in `hub`. Keep the member's store outside the upstream checkout, or, when it must sit inside, list it in `.git/info/exclude` (never committed) rather than `.gitignore` (committed). Never run `reflow2 init` in a repository you do not own. The pin is `external_dependency` with the member's graph id and how it is watched. Under the door, pass `--export-to` on every member write.
(b) SPLIT BY WHAT IT IS ABOUT: the store-placement rule goes where the accepted "design lives apart" intent is served (getting started, adopt, init), because it holds for any design over code its owner does not control, not only hub members. `hub` keeps the pin's shape and points there.
(c) WAIT for the address book (dec:idea-a-hub-on-one-machine-can-say-where-each-tracked-design-is-reached-from-the-door) and the one-call member tool (dec:idea-one-call-adds-a-member-design-to-a-local-hub). Either would change what the procedure says.

SIZE: small. Skill text, its mirrors and the skill lint. No code.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, kept beside it:
- `.git/info/exclude` is git plumbing, and the accepted intent is that the design does not live in the code repository at all. Teaching how to hide a store INSIDE someone else's checkout may normalise the case the intent moves away from.
- The pin's shape is the tool's schema, which `--describe external_dependency` serves since 0.78.0. Prose restating a schema goes stale when the schema moves.
- "Export after every member write" is mostly the 0.78.0 door's job now. As a rule it asks the agent to do what the binary does, except where no export is named anywhere, which may be the one sentence worth adding.
- The work hub already has this as its own project skill. A served copy helps the next local hub driven through the door.
properties.name: OPEN — should the served hub skill teach how a member design is kept under the --call door: where its store lives and how it stays out of an upstream repository's git, the pin's shape, and an export after every member write?
